extractions.value: TMS variables were recorded, during monitoring of the silence of the EMG activity in the right arm (in the intervals between SPS attacks), by placing the figure-of-eight coil on the left primary motor cortex and recording motor evoked potentials (MEPs) from the right abductor pollicis brevis (ABP) muscle, according to international guidelines. Resting motor threshold (RMT) (i.e., the percentage of the maximal stimulator output (monophasic Magstim Bi-Stim) eliciting MEPs of at least 50 lV with 50% probability). For short-latency afferent inhibition (SAI), the conditioning stimulus was an electric pulse delivered on the median nerve at wrist, at an intensity producing a nonpainful thumb twitch. The test stimulus was a suprathreshold single TMS pulse evoking, when unconditioned, a stable MEP in the ABP muscle of 800–1000 lV. The interstimulus interval (ISI) between the two stimuli was 21 ms. For cortical silent period (CSP), ten single suprathreshold (130% of the RMT) TMS pulses (ISI [ 7-s) were delivered on the contralateral motor cortex. Short-latency intracortical inhibition (SICI) and intracortical facilitation (ICF) were obtained by paired-pulse TMS with randomized ISIs of 2, 4, 6 (SICI) and 8, 10, 12 (ICF) ms (conditioning stimulus 80% of RMT, test stimulus as for SAI). Classical indices of spinal excitability, obtained with conventional procedures in right median nerve. The startle response, obtained by sudden acoustic stimulation and surface EMG recordings from neck, trunk and limb muscles.
